div.div: رَغْدٌ , applied to property, or water, or life, or herbage, Plentiful; that does not cause one fatigue. (L.) [Being originally an inf. n., it is used without variation as a masc. and fem. and sing. and pl. epithet; as also ↓ رَغَدٌ .] You say عَيْشٌ رَغْدٌ and ↓ رَغَدٌ and ↓ رَاغِدٌ and ↓ رَغِيدٌ (A, Msb) and ↓ أَرْغَدُ , (Lh, TA,) and ↓ مَعِيشَةٌ رَغِيدَةٌ , (A,) Life that is ample in its means or circumstances, unstraitened, or plentiful, (Lh, A, Msb,) and easy, (Lh, * Msb,) and pleasant. (A, Msb.) And غِيشَةٌ رَغْدٌ and ↓ رَغَدٌ A mode of life ample in its means or circumstances, unstraitened, or plentiful, [and easy,] and pleasant. (S, A, K.) And ↓ قَوْمٌ رَغَدٌ , (A, L, K,) or رَغْدٌ, (JK,) and ↓ نِسْوَةٌ رَغَدٌ , (A, L, K,) or نِسَآءٌ رَغْدٌ, (JK,) People, and women, in a state of life ample in its means or circumstances, &c.; (JK, A, K;) or having abundance of herbage, or of the goods, conveniences, or comforts, of life, and having camels abounding with milk. (L.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
